sentences.text: Fallacosteus was an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm that lived during the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
This species possessed an elongated snout that likely improved its hydrodynamic streamlining.
Fossils of Fallacosteus have been found in the Gogo Formation in Kimberley, Western Australia.
The specific name turneri honors Sue Turner.
Fallacosteus belongs to the family Camuropiscidae, the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, and the clade Coccosteomorphi.
Fallacosteus was a marine genus described scientifically by Long in 1990.
Fallacosteus lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
